families.family: Cisco (formerly Scientific-Atlanta) GainMaker 1 GHz amplifiers: System Amplifier HGD, LGD, HGBT (standard GaAs, High Output and GaN variants) and Line Extender (manual, thermal, AGC), 42/54 and 65/86 MHz splits
families.controlsSummary: On 1 GHz GainMaker System Amplifiers (HGD, LGD, HGBT and the HO/GaN versions) and Line Extenders, forward output level and output tilt are set only with fixed-value plug-in parts. Nothing electronic is used to choose level or tilt. Level: the forward input pad slot takes a plug-in attenuator, 0 to 20.5 dB in 0.5 dB steps (GM-PAD-1G-xx=, legacy 589693-589734); a higher pad gives lower output. Tilt: the forward input EQ slot takes a 1 GHz cable EQ (0 dB jumper 4007228, then 1.5 to 30 dB in 1.5 dB steps, 4007229-4007248). At short-spaced locations it takes an inverse EQ instead (4007486-4007495, marked 1.6/1.5 to 16.2/15.0 dB). A higher cable-EQ value pulls the low end down relative to 870 MHz/1 GHz. Separate 870 MHz cable EQs (589260-589278) let the station run as an 870 MHz design. The factory fits the plug-in interstage EQ and the interstage and output pads to set gain and internal tilt; they are not chosen in the field. Data sheets give 10.5 dB ISEQ for HGD/LGD/HGBT, 9 dB for manual and AGC line extenders and 7.5 dB for thermal line extenders. Thermal and AGC stations add an interstage Bode network, a DC-controlled variable loss and slope. Three-position switch S1 selects what drives it. AGC stations: position 1 is thermal setup, 2 is manual setup (MANUAL BACKOFF pot), 3 is AGC operation. Thermal stations: 1 is amplifier-only, 3 is amplifier+coax, and 2 is not used. In AGC manual setup, the backoff pot is turned to full gain, then backed off by an amount read from a temperature chart, before tilt and level are set. After the plug-ins are chosen, an AGC pad from the same pad set is fitted: main-port output at the pilot minus 34 dB on system amplifiers, minus 29 dB on line extenders. The AGC GAIN pot is then trimmed so the level does not change between the setup and operate positions. Data sheets give an auto slope and gain range of +/-5.5 dB (+/-5 dB on the 65/86 line extender). Manual line extenders have no Bode, so S1 does nothing. HGD/LGD also take a plug-in signal director (jumper, splitter, DC-8 or DC-12) that sets the aux-port loss. A SYS TRIM slot takes an optional trim network for response shaping; after fitting one, the interstage or input pad is changed to restore level. Return path: reverse input and output pads come from the same pad set. The reverse cable EQ steps 0 to 12 dB in 1 dB steps: 42 MHz EQs for 42/54 and 65 MHz EQs for 65/86.

items.appliesTo: GainMaker forward cable equalizers (1002, 870, 750 MHz) and inverse equalizers
items.values: (1) 716336 Rev D: a forward cable EQ's 'dB value' is the equivalent cable length, in dB at the rated high frequency (750, 870 or 1002 MHz), that it is designed to offset. The value and rated frequency are printed on top of the EQ, and the tilt it produces from low to high frequency is printed on its side. An inverse EQ's value is the cable length in dB that would produce similar tilt. (2) Data sheets: 'Available in 1.5 dB steps from 0 to 30 dB at 1002 MHz'. (3) OL-31156-01 'To Set the Output Tilt': EQs come in 1.5 dB (equivalent) increments, and a 1.5 dB change moves the low-to-high difference by approximately 1 dB. A higher EQ value lowers the low frequencies relative to 870 MHz/1 GHz; a lower value raises them. (4) OL-31155-01 adds 'approximately 1 dB generally, or 1.2 dB for AGC stations in manual setup mode'. (5) The OL-31156-01 p.96 'Total Tilt (52-1000 MHz)' column runs 1.2, 2.4, 3.6 ... 24.0 for EQ values 1.5, 3.0, 4.5 ... 30.0.

The column order 52, 70, 55, 86 is printed that way in both independent extractions (Exa of the Cisco PDF and Firecrawl of the mirror), so it is not a parsing artifact. items.appliesTo: 1 GHz GainMaker System Amplifiers (HGD, LGD, HGBT, HO and GaN)
items.values: The interstage EQ is fixed, not chosen in the field. It is factory-installed, should not be changed in the field, and is a 1 GHz EQ suitable for both 1 GHz and 870 MHz systems. The plug-in interstage EQ and an on-board interstage EQ together give the station's total internal tilt, and the plug-in value differs between amplifier types by design. The forward aux output, interstage and main output pads are factory-installed to set operational gain and should not be changed unless system design requires it. Tilt is set with the forward input EQ or inverse EQ and level with the forward input pad (pp.54-55). The trim-network procedure (p.71, step 7) is the one place the guide says to change the interstage pad or input pad, to restore the earlier output level. Data sheets give 'Auto/Thermal with 10.5 dB I/S EQ' for HGD, LGD and HGBT in 42/54 and 65/86, and for the HO HGD and GaN HGBT 85/102 sheets.

items.values: Order: tilt first with the forward input EQ, then level at the highest frequency with the forward input pad, then AGC alignment. (0) Configure per the design print and warm up about one hour. Pick the procedure (p.51) and set S1. AGC manual setup: S1 position 2; turn MANUAL BACKOFF fully counterclockwise for maximum gain, then clockwise to cut output by the Manual Backoff Chart amount for the current temperature and reference frequency, and do not touch it again. AGC thermal setup: S1 position 1. Thermal amplifier-only: S1 position 1. Thermal amplifier+coax: S1 position 3. (1) Verify input at the forward input test point at the lowest and highest design frequencies, adding 20 dB for the test point (pp.49-50). (2) Find output tilt at the forward main output test point as the dB difference between the lowest and highest specified frequencies. (3) Set tilt with the forward input EQ or inverse EQ. Within +/-0.5 dB of design tilt, move on. Tilt more than design: fit a lower EQ value. Tilt less than design: fit a higher one. Re-measure. (4) Set level: measure at the highest design frequency. Within +/-0.5 dB of design level, move on. Above design: fit a higher-value forward input pad. Below design: fit a lower one. Repeat. On HGD/LGD, the aux test points read after the signal director. (5) AGC stations: AGC pad = main-port output at pilot frequency minus 34 dB (UBT minus 26 dB). Note the pilot level in the setup position, set S1 to 3, adjust AGC GAIN to match, and toggle S1 between the setup position and 3 until the level does not change. Leave S1 at 3. (6) Amplifier+coax thermal station balanced without warm-up: set output 1 dB below the design level (+/-0.5 dB).

items.values: Same order as the System Amplifier. S1 positions are the same: AGC stations 1 thermal setup, 2 manual setup, 3 AGC operate; thermal stations 1 amplifier-only, 2 not used, 3 amplifier+coax. Verify input at the lowest and highest design frequencies. Set tilt with the forward input EQ: within +/-0.5 dB of design tilt; more than design means a lower EQ, less means a higher EQ. Then set level at the highest design frequency with the forward input pad: within +/-0.5 dB; above design means a higher pad, below means a lower pad. Then AGC alignment with AGC pad = RF output level at pilot frequency (output port) minus 29 dB. LE wording: a 1.5 dB EQ change moves the low-to-high difference by approximately 1 dB generally, or 1.2 dB for AGC stations in manual setup mode. Manual stations have no Bode and S1 has no effect; the same tilt-then-level steps apply. Amplifier+coax thermal stations have a cold-amplifier procedure: set the design level minus 1 dB, +/-0.5 dB.

families.controlsSummary: HGD and HGBT set forward input level and tilt electronically, not with plug-in pads and EQs chosen in the field. The LE datasheets point the same way but give no detail. The tech starts the QuantumLink Local app on an Android or iOS device and pairs it over Bluetooth with the QuantumLink Local Wireless Interface plugged into the module. The app loads the downstream profile (pilot frequencies and power levels; the guide says AGC pilot frequencies are user-defined when ordering). The tech then runs a downstream auto-alignment. An optional manual alignment can follow, which steps pilot-frequency power levels until the level markers match the reference markers. The SA guide (V02102025) says three things about this. The amp sets itself to unity gain within the network's RF design with no field level measurements. All SAs should have identical output levels, with the varying RF inputs adjusted electronically. Levels are not adjusted in the field after the initial installation. ALSC is off by default and is turned on for each amp after downstream and upstream alignment. The guide also lists factory-installed 'Forward Universal Trim' parts, one shipping at 0 dB and one at 6 dB. Its HGD photo shows a single plug-in socket labelled 'Universal Trim', but the guide never says whether the trim is a pad or an equalizer, and it lists no other values. The HGD, HGBT and LE datasheets only say that forward gain and noise figure were measured with an equivalent 0 dB input EQ and a 1 dB input pad setting. No AOI document found, live or archived, gives a range, step or reference frequencies for the electronic input attenuation or equalization. The BA works differently: it uses plug-in pads. AOI's English BA datasheet v08302024 (PRELIMINARY) is no longer on AOI's site and was read from Internet Archive snapshots of AOI's own URL. It says a 0 dB pad is installed and that 2, 4 and 6 dB pads are stored in the lid for gain adjustment. The live Spanish edition of the same version cuts this note short. No BA EQ options, pad part numbers or pad loss-vs-frequency data were found. No installation guide for the LE or the BA is public, and AOI's product page now offers datasheets and installation guides only on request. Result: the only pad or EQ value set with manufacturer provenance is the BA forward pad set of 0, 2, 4 and 6 dB, from a preliminary, withdrawn, archive-sourced datasheet. For HGD, HGBT and LE there are no plug-in values the solver can offer and no published electronic range or step.

items.appliesTo: Quantum18 HGD and HGBT (guide says the process is the same for both; illustrated with HGD)
items.values: 1) Splice the amp in per field practice; the tech device runs the QuantumLink Local Mobile Application. 2) Insert the QuantumLink Local Wireless Interface into the module, pair over Bluetooth with 'Select Device', log in. 3) Menu > About: check wireless-interface firmware, app version, MAC. 4) Amplifier Info tile: check or update alias and description. 5) Amplifier Config tile: check diplex filter split (pick from the drop-down if wrong); ALSC defaults to OFF; Operational Mode defaults to 1.8GHz (1.2GHz selectable); firmware bank/update. 6) Location Data (GPS, Google Maps or manual lat/long). 7) DS Auto Config tile: Auto Config updates frequency settings and power levels for this amp's profile; ALSC and Auto Align Marker Pilots are for information only; select Apply. 8) DS Align tile > Auto > Start Downstream Alignment, after pilot frequencies are confirmed and stored. 9) Optional DS Manual alignment, only after auto-alignment: adjust values one at a time until Level Marker frequency levels match Ref. Marker levels; the check box applies changes without saving; Save Configuration saves; Revert returns to the factory preset so DS Auto Align overrides manual changes. Guide says this is typically not needed in normal field conditions. 10) Spectrum tile: about 30 s scan of the DS output to verify. 11) Upstream alignment after DS setup of the whole cascade, starting at the last amp (Auto, or Manual with Gain and Tilt adjustments using a Viavi ONX-630 in DOCSIS Expert mode). 12) Cascade ALSC activation: Amplifier Config > ALSC ON, repeat for every amp in the cascade.
